UNITED NATIONS DEVELOPMENT ASSISTANCE FRAMEWORK (UNDAF)
GEORGIA
2006-2010
United Nations Country Team in Georgia
March 2005
  TABLE OF CONTENTS  
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The UNDAF is the result of a consultative process between the UN Agencies, the Government of Georgia, civil society and other partners aiming to respond to national priorities and needs. The UNDAF is guided by the principles of the Georgian Millenium Development Goals Report (MDGR) and the Economic Development and Poverty Reduction Programme (EDPRP) and is based upon the Common Country Assessment (CCA) completed by the UNCT in August 2004. The UNDAF translates the combined objectives from these analyses into a common operational framework for development activities upon which the individual United Nations Agencies, Funds and Programmes will formulate their action for the period 2006-2010.  
The UNDAF thus describes the United Nations planned assistance to the people and Government of Georgia between 2006 and 2010. During the UNDAF Prioritisation Retreat attended by the UN Agencies, Government, civil society and academia in September 2004, five inter-related areas of cooperation were agreed upon as being particularly critical for Georgia. These areas are listed as: (1) Poverty and Economic Growth, (2) Governance, (3) Basic Social Services, (4) Volatility and Instability and (5) Environment.
The UNDAF Outcomes emerging from these five thematic areas were then linked closely to Country Programme Outcomes and Outputs, as summarised in the UNDAF Results Matrices at pages 12 - 20. From the UNDAF will flow the individual UN Country Programme documents containing the detail and schedule of programme activity to be conducted during the five year UNDAF cycle. The UNDAF contents were endorsed by the Government, civil society and other partners at a Joint Strategy Meeting (JSM) on 28 February 2005.
All UNDAF related activity will be conducted within the context of the United Nation’s human rights-based approach and UN perspectives on gender equality. The UNDAF is a living document which may be updated or adjusted at any time during its five year duration to take into account developments or changes in the Georgian context.
Progress in achieving the planned UNDAF Outcomes will be measured through the UNDAF Monitoring and Evaluation process,  which links Outcomes with relevant indicators and sources of verification. These are summarised in the Monitoring & Evaluation Tables at pages 22 - 29. There will be two major reviews of the UNDAF process during the five year cycle. A midterm review will be conducted in 2008 and a final UNDAF evaluation in 2009, in time to inform planning for a future UNDAF cycle. Throughout the cycle UNDAF activity will be monitored and evaluated in regular meetings of the UNCT-led working groups comprising UN Agencies, Government, civil society and other partners. 
The UNDAF provides a roadmap for focused and coordinated development assistance and activity in Georgia. In the dynamic post Rose Revolution climate the Georgian people must urgently and energetically address their national priorities and commitments to Millenium Development Goals, including Poverty Reduction. With the continued support of the United Nations and other partners it is hoped that Georgia will achieve the necessary transition from relief to development - and with it, a more secure and equable future for all Georgians.
PREAMBLE
The present United Nations Development Assistance Framework (UNDAF) has been developed through consultation with the United Nations Country Team (UNCT) in Georgia, the Georgian Government, the Civil Society, the Academia and the Donor Community with the aim of improving the lives of the people of Georgia, especially the most vulnerable.
In cooperation with the Government and other development partners, the UNCT will support Georgia’s fulfillment of the Millennium Development Goals (MDG) and the objectives set out in the Economic Development and Poverty Reduction Programme  (EDPRP), as well as the country’s commitment to international conventions and summits. 
The UNCT aims to assist the people of Georgia in their quest for a better future - one which provides equal opportunity for all.
UNDAF at a glance
  Poverty and Economic Growth                       Governance                                                      Basic Social Services                                           Volatility and Instability                                Environment                                      
I. INTRODUCTION
Background and Purpose
In order for the United Nations to articulate a coherent vision and strategy for a unified approach towards common development goals at the country level, the Common Country Assessment (CCA) and United Nations Development Assistance Framework (UNDAF) were adopted as strategic planning tools for the UN system intended to enhance the UN’s collective analysis and programming in support of national goals and priorities. The CCA and UNDAF are designed to assist the UN Country Team with the preparation of country programs and projects supported by UN agencies.
In the third quarter of 2004, the UN Country Team in Georgia (UNCT) finalised the CCA document which prepared the ground for the UNDAF process. Five themes: (1) Poverty and Economic Growth  (2) Governance  (3) Basic Social Services  (4) Volatility and Instability and  (5) Environment have been selected as the basis around which our future programmes will be structured. These themes are also being addressed in a human rights and gender sensitive context.
The development of the UNDAF was consultative and included submissions from all the UN agencies represented within the UNCT (UNDP, UNFAO, UNFPA, UNHCR, UNICEF, UNIFEM, UNOCHA, UNV, UNWFP, WHO and IOM), as well as from representatives of the Georgian Government, civil society, academia and the donor community.  The UN’s Regional Support Team also provided feedback and support during the UNDAF development process.
Process Overview / Methodology
In September 2004, the UNCT held a UNDAF Prioritization Retreat led by a UN Staff College facilitator and two resource officers. Thematic working groups were set up for the five areas of cooperation: (1) Poverty and Economic Growth, (2) Governance, (3) Basic Social Services, (4) Volatility and Instability, and (5) Environment.  Agreement on the UNDAF outcomes was considered a major achievement of the Retreat. Subsequent UNDAF working group meetings produced a first draft of the Results and the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) matrices at the end of October. These were then finalised during meetings between the Regional Support Team and UNDAF working groups in November. The first drafts of the UNDAF Results and M&E matrices were then forwarded for comment to the Regional Readers Group in December 2004.
Given the importance of a Human Rights Based Approach (HRBA) to our work, the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) sensitised the UNCT to International Human Rights Law and the Georgian National Legal Framework. This workshop took place in June 2004, prior to the initiation of the CCA/UNDAF process and helped participants to analyse the country’s development situation from a human rights-based perspective.
II. 	AREAS OF COOPERATION
As noted, the United Nations system in Georgia has selected five themes that have been translated into UNDAF outcomes. These themes are:  (1) Poverty and Economic Growth,  (2) Governance, (3) Basic Social Services (Health, Child/Family Welfare, Education), (4) Volatility and Instability and (5) Environment. Table A, the UNDAF Results Matrix, provides details on the Country Programme Outcomes that will contribute to each UNDAF Outcome, the Country Programme Outputs (products, services, skills, or abilities) and the partners with whom the UN agencies will cooperate. This section describes the critical choices made during the preparation of the UNDAF and their rationale.
In addition to the five major areas of cooperation, crosscutting issues such as gender equality, the empowerment of women, combating HIV/AIDS, civil society development, and respect for human rights - are objectives that the UN agencies will pursue in the course of their activities during 2006-2010. These crosscutting issues form an integral part of each of the National Priorities and UNDAF Outcomes.
(1) Poverty And Economic Growth
Poverty and food insecurity in Georgia have not improved significantly since the socio-economic downturn following independence, because their underlying causes have not been sufficiently addressed. Rapid and sustainable economic growth and a significant improvement in the population’s social situation remains the continuing challenge confronting the Georgians. 
Key documents including the Millenium Development Goals Report (MDG), the Economic Development and Poverty Reduction Programme (EDPRP) and the Sustainable Agriculture Development and Food Security Strategy - point to the centrality of effective and sustainable economic and agricultural development to reduced poverty and improved food security. The United Nations sees several opportunities to support the implementation of the Poverty Reduction strategy. UN Agencies and particularly UNDP will work in close cooperation with the Government to increase its capacity for efficient implementation of the EDPRP. This may include assisting to improve coordination between the line ministries and the Ministry of Economic Development during the decision-making process and implementation. Assistance in monitoring the implementation of the EDPRP will also be provided through a UN database / software system, DevInfo.
The United Nations will promote decentralised decision-making and greater resource allocation to allow communities to develop appropriate and sustainable responses to their needs.  It will continue to assist in the creation and rehabilitation of agricultural assets and infrastructure in targeted communities. The UN will help expand support to small scale farmers, most of whom are poor, vulnerable and food insecure, through improved access to, and efficient use of, resources and external markets, through the provision of seeds and livestock and the development of local credit schemes and capacities in farming and animal husbandry.  UNHCR will engage refugees in local integration development projects.
In parallel with the above medium and long-term interventions, the UN will support the adoption and implementation of Government and joint social protection mechanisms to address the immediate needs of verified vulnerable population groups (pensioners, elderly, children in institutions, disabled and the other disadvantaged groups). It will seek to improve needs-based targeting methodology and enhance support to equitable social protection reforms, including child welfare system reform.
(2) Governance
Following the Rose Revolution in November 2003, the new government in Georgia launched a massive reform effort, aimed at improving governance in general and combating corruption in particular. This reform process was initiated against a background characterised by the absence of the rule of law, a lack of clarity on the roles and responsibilities of the various government sectors, a lack of efficient management, long-term planning and broad participation. Although the results of such reforms are starting to be visible, many of the underlying problems remain and require further effort.
There are various types of problems in the governance sector that are summarised in the paragraph below. Internal systems within the government, particularly the clarification of powers and competencies between central and local levels and the establishment of a professional and impartial civil service, remain deficient. Oversight of the government is in the very initial stages and public participation in decision-making, although increasing, is not yet institutionalised. Crosscutting concerns relate to data generation and analysis, capacity building of the government, gender equality, independence of the three powers (Executive, Legislative and Judiciary) and respect for Human Rights.
Thus, Georgia needs to tackle its governance reforms via three different but interrelated angles: 
(1) efficiency and effectiveness of the delivery of public services, with a special focus on local government (2) transparency and accountability of the Executive, Legislative and Judiciary    
(3) stronger public participation, with a special focus on gender, youth, minorities and elderly.
The United Nations programmes will provide assistance in the development of the necessary governance systems for all three areas, with a particular focus on strengthening the capacity of local government units, bringing government closer to the citizens, and the inclusion of vulnerable groups. There will also be a particular focus on oversight mechanisms, be it institutional oversight or civil society oversight, as well as on overall strengthening of the rule of law. A final focus of the UN assistance will be on policy making capacities and processes at all levels of government. 
(3) Basic Social Services
Within the turmoil of the post Soviet socio-economic transition, the systems and quality of basic social services (health, child/family welfare and education, in particular) have been affected by collapsing infrastructure, overcapacity of certain institutional and human resources versus inefficient management, low budget allotments, and decreased funding. The impact of the economic crisis on the disruption of social services, together with increased poverty, limited the accessibility of healthcare and education for the general population and overemphasised the institutionalisation of vulnerable populations as a viable assistance strategy. The deterioration of the infrastructure and management networks has been further compromised by lack of results-oriented policies and long-term strategies with a vague planning framework incapable of reversing the downturn. 
Through analysis of the existing social service systems and bottlenecks, quality and accessibility of the population to basic social services have been identified as key challenges. 
In terms of health, increasing national capacities for ensuring the fulfillment of the population’s rights to basic health services, quality and accessibility of RH services, enhancement of existing national responses to HIV/AIDS, TB and Malaria and the promotion of adequate nutrition have been major programme outcomes prioritised by the UN Country Team (UNCT). The UN contribution towards attainment of the national development goals within the health system will be mainstreamed through advocacy, institutional and human capacity development and programme communication strategies. 
Child welfare reform will emphasise the movement from an institution based system of child welfare to community based services. Policy, standards and programmes promoting a social and family environment for the cognitive, social and emotional development of children will be undertaken within the child welfare system resulting in reduced reliance on residential institutions and increased community based family/child welfare services. Regarding education, one UNDAF priority will be the inclusion of life skills education into the national curriculum as well as ensuring increased access of marginalised groups to formal and informal education opportunities. This priority will serve as a basis for UN advocacy and policy development assistance. 
(4) Volatility and Instability
The UNDAF outcome for this section focuses on two main areas that have an impact on the country’s stability: man-made conflicts and natural disasters. Their prevention, or at least mitigation, are not adequately addressed by the Government due to limited capacity in this field. 
Underlying causes for instability include weak governance, general poverty and a dire socio-economic situation, especially in conflict-affected areas. UNCT programmes will focus on capacity building, accompanied by advocacy and awareness raising efforts addressing tolerance, human rights, minority and IDP/refugee rights in the general public as well as in conflict affected populations. Special attention will be given to recovery and rehabilitation projects for IDPs and local communities by restoring basic services, rehabilitating infrastructure and improving the economic situation. 
Given the current political and socio-economic situation, the presence of two unresolved conflicts, a history of civil unrest and protest and the existence of other “conflict-prone or unstable” regions, emphasis will be placed on conflict transformation efforts. Examples will include the enhancement of dialogue between parties, the protection of human rights, the promotion of durable solutions for displaced populations and the economic rehabilitation and recovery efforts beneficial to reconciliation and/or future conflict prevention. In parallel to the above, the United Nations will continue its active participation in peace processes regarding Abkhazia and South Ossetia.  
Another concern is the very limited natural disaster management capacity at the national level. Since Georgia is a disaster prone country, with hazards such as earthquake, droughts and floods, the requirement to strengthen the Government’s preparedness and response capacity is of utmost importance. Therefore, UN agency programmes will focus on initiatives to build this capacity.
Coordination efforts between the government agencies, the UN and civil society should be strengthened and humanitarian concerns should not be limited to a single point on the hypothetical “relief to development continuum”.  Rather, the complexity of the Georgian context requires simultaneous action across a range of humanitarian related concerns.
The issue of the relief to development continuum and the promotion of transitional programmes directed more towards the development sector, is emphasised. The coordination mechanism between the UN, international and local organizations, and government, should be strengthened. These issues cut across all the thematic areas described in the UNDAF matrix. 
(5) Environment
Georgia recognises environmental protection as one of the national priorities. The long-term strategic document “Economic Development and Poverty Reduction Program” states the improvement of environmental condition by the year 2015 as one of the major national goals. In addition the country has adopted the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) and is at least formally committed to the achievement of these goals by the year 2015, including MDG7 – to ensure environmental sustainability. The United Nations Development Assistance Framework (UNDAF) in the area of environment reflects these national goals and commitments and takes into consideration the collective comparative advantage of the UN system in achieving MDGs.
Thus the UNDAF will contribute to the achievement of national environmental goals and MDG7, specifically Target 14: “Integrate the principles of sustainable development into country policies and programmes and reverse the loss of environmental resources” with an outcome to be demonstrated progress towards ensuring environmental sustainability. This UNDAF outcome will be attained through building national and local capacities and adopting sustainable practices for environmental and natural resource management. The related Country Programme Outcomes are largely based on CCA analysis.  Amongst others; unsustainable practices of natural resource management, poor capacity for local and global environmental management, low level of integration of environmental considerations into development and sectoral policy and planning, low environmental awareness, an imperfect legal-institutional framework, were identified as immediate, underlying and basic causes for the degradation of the natural environment in Georgia. The UN Country Programme will contribute to eradicating these causes and reversing or at least halting the negative trend of degradation in the natural environment.  These outcomes will be attained through the Country Program Outputs described below.
CP Outcome 1:  The national and local capacities for sustainable environment and natural resource management will be enhanced through:
improving the legal-institutional basis and intervention at the policy level, raising the awareness of key decision makers and civil society on sustainable development and environmental sustainability;
increasing the national capacities for environmental monitoring and the implementation of major UN environmental conventions, including the conventions on climate change, biodiversity protection, land degradation and ozone layer protection; 
empowering the government in financial resource mobilisation and utilisation for environmental protection and;
strengthening the capacities of civil society for sustainable environmental management through the  implementation of the GEF Small Grants Program.
CP Outcome 2: Sustainable environmental and natural resource practices will be promoted and adopted through the implemention of pilot projects, multiplying their successes nationwide, and intervention at the policy level. The focus will be on integrated river basin management, sustainable land resource management, the protection and sustainable use of biodiversity, the expansion and strengthening of protected area systems and the increased use of indigenous renewable energy resources.
III.	IMPLEMENTATION
The UNCT plans to keep the existing CCA/UNDAF Theme Groups to coordinate and manage the implementation of the UNDAF. The five Theme Groups, namely Poverty and Economic Growth, Governance, Basic Social Services, Volatility and Instability and Environment will focus on the relevant National Priorities. 
The Theme Groups will report to the UNCT.  Their terms of reference will include reviewing joint work plans, reviewing monitoring and evaluation activities, and ensuring information sharing. All UN agencies will be encouraged to participate in all meetings of the Theme Groups, and the relevant and interested stakeholders will be invited. Taskforces on cross-cutting issues such as Gender, Human Rights and HIV/AIDS will be formed as needed.
IV.		MONITORING AND EVALUATION (M&E)
UNDAF M&E Plan: The UNDAF Theme Groups prepared the UNDAF M&E Plan approved by the UNCT. The Theme Groups will be responsible for the implementation of the M&E plan and will report to the UNCT on this matter.
UNDAF Midterm Review: The UNCT has agreed to undertake an UNDAF Midterm Review in 2008 to assess achievements and shortcomings and to identify strategies for the remaining UNDAF period. The midterm review will ensure that the UNDAF remains relevant to the EDPRP and the national MDGs. 
Final UNDAF Evaluation: In 2009 (the second last year of the UNDAF), the UNCT will conduct a joint and final UNDAF Evaluation. The Final Evaluation will assess the results of the UNDAF in terms of :
(1) impact and sustainability of impact  (2) relevance to Georgia’s pursuit of the MDGs, EDPRP targets and other development commitments  (3) positioning within the development community  (4)  effectiveness in contributing to the intended outcomes and (5) the efficiency and effectiveness of the UNDAF as a coordination framework.
Coordination and Management of M&E: The UNCT will coordinate the monitoring and evaluation of the UNDAF by arranging surveys, joint field visits, outcome evaluations and other mechanisms. Stakeholders from the Government, civil society, and the international community will be invited to participate in these activities as appropriate. The groups and individuals assigned to perform M&E tasks will report their findings to the UNCT through the M&E Working Groups.
Strengthening national M&E capacity: The EDPRP and CCA identify a number of areas where national M&E capacity building is needed. Accordingly the UNCT, in cooperation with other partners, will continue supporting the data collection, research, and monitoring functions of the Government (including DevInfo training and support), throughout the UNDAF period. This support aims to enable effective national monitoring of progress toward the MDGs and EDPRP targets, subsequent national development strategies, and other international instruments to which Georgia is a party.  The UNDAF Monitoring and Evaluation process will remain closely aligned with national processes.   
Risks and Assumptions: The UNCT made a number of assumptions in preparing the UNDAF. These assumptions, and the risks related to them, may affect the achievement of the Outcomes. The assumptions include the following:
Macroeconomic stability continues
Political stability continues
Conflicts do not resume/escalate
Changes in the regional and international political environment do not have adverse impacts on socioeconomic conditions in Georgia
Social development receives priority attention from the side of government and donors.
